searchText: b"h remaining work — geelooy runtime, api, ui, and deployment audit the awtsmoos renews each instant; this ledger renews each obligation in sight. no route is called complete while errors still burn in the night. awtsmoos.com is the vessel under inspection, with evidence as the light. mission audit every discoverable page under geelooy, remove runtime failures, repair /apps, improve shared apis and ui architecture where evidence justifies it, verify movie friendly responsive css, then commit and push all repository changes requested by the user and prove the deployed url live. observed evidence repository root: /users/awtsmoos/work/awtsmoos.com. target surface: geelooy/ with many route families including apps, api, auth, social, editors, games, docs, os, and shared ui. user screenshot shows /apps loading a javascript module request that receives application/json, plus 404s for foundation.js and favicon.ico. root agents.md requires inspection before claims, real provider verification, complete file rewrites, small modules, and real tests. tunnel is connected and execution healthy; a stale outbox receipt exists but current filesystem requests succeed. known work graph [ ] capture clean git branch, head, remotes, status, and unrelated modifications. [ ] inventory route entrypoints beneath geelooy. [ ] inventory javascript module entrypoints and static asset references. [ ] inventory api facing client modules and server api routes used by geelooy pages. [ ] reproduce /apps in chrome and capture console/network failures. [ ] identify the exact request returning json for a module script and prove why. [ ] find every broken local static import, missing asset, bad relative url, and route to file mismatch. [ ] build or strengthen automated route/runtime auditing so regressions are caught repeatedly. [ ] audit shared ui foundations before duplicating page local fixes. [ ] audit css loading, responsive behavior, typography, controls, focus states, overlays, and cinematic/mobile layouts. [ ] improve api organization only where actual usage, duplication, weak validation, or inconsistent contracts are observed. [ ] rewrite every touched source file completely; no partial textual patching. [ ] keep touched executable source files small; split real responsibilities into coherent modules. [ ] use tabs, readable formatting, complete jsdoc with every parameter, return value, failure mode, and useful awtsmoos poetry. [ ] add or update tests for every repaired public/runtime contract. [ ] run syntax, lint, test, build, import resolution, and page runtime checks available in the repository. [ ] crawl every practical page route with browser/runtime auditing and record clean/error results. [ ] verify /apps specifically has zero relevant console/runtime errors and no broken module requests. [ ] read back every touched file fully after implementation. [ ] compare planned versus actual changes and close all deltas. [ ] re run git status and inspect every repository change, including unrelated pre existing work. [ ] commit all changes requested by the user without discarding unrelated work. [ ] push the correct branch/remotes to github. [ ] determine actual deployment mechanism from repository evidence. [ ] deploy through the repository's real production path. [ ] verify the deployed url directly, including /apps and representative page families. [ ] confirm the published/live receipt or equivalent evidence before reporting deployment success. risks to track route enumeration may include dynamic parameterized pages that require fixtures or authentication. some browser errors may originate from extensions rather than site code; classify by source before fixing. broad api rewrites can break public contracts; preserve signatures and response shapes unless all consumers migrate together. user requested pushing unrelated work; inspect it before committing so secrets, local artifacts, or destructive debris are not published blindly. deployment may have multiple targets; derive the canonical target from config, github workflow, or hosting scripts. next action capture git status/branch/remotes, inspect the apps and shared runtime trees, then reproduce /apps in chrome before any source rewrite.
